title: Extension of an integral space across a quasi-compact open
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Work with algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], with atlas topology on field-valued point classes [def-a1-space-point-topology] and sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. A geometric point is a map $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$ from an algebraically closed field [def-weil-geometric-point], and its geometric fibre is the sheaf fibre product with this map. Quasi-compact means quasi-compact on scheme tests, or, for a space, that every open cover has a finite subcover. Quasi-separated means that the absolute diagonal over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is quasi-compact. Separated for a morphism means that its diagonal is representable by closed immersions [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Etale means representable etale on scheme tests [def-trf-algebraic-space, def-weil-etale-morphism]. Integral means representable and integral on scheme tests [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]; in particular its pullback to an affine scheme is affine. Open immersions are representable by open immersions on scheme tests [def-weil-open-immersion]. Let $V\hookrightarrow B$ be a quasi-compact open immersion and let $Z\to V$ be integral. There are an algebraic space $E$, an integral morphism $E\to B$, and an isomorphism $E\times_BV\simeq Z$ over $V$. Under this isomorphism $Z\hookrightarrow E$ is the pullback open immersion.

proof.text: Write $j:V\hookrightarrow B$ and $\pi:Z\to V$, and set $f=j\pi$. By [lem-sfb-space-integral-qcqs-permanence], $\pi$ is quasi-compact and separated. The open immersion $j$ is a monomorphism: on any scheme test two lifts have the same image in the open subscheme and hence are equal. Its diagonal is therefore an isomorphism, in particular a closed immersion; thus $j$ is separated. By [lem-sfb-space-separated-fp-composition], $f$ is separated.

Quasi-compactness of $j$ and of $f$ is meant on scheme tests, as in the statement and in the hypothesis of the factorization node applied in step 3. Let $T$ be a quasi-compact scheme with a map $T\to B$. Since $j$ is a representable open immersion that is quasi-compact on scheme tests, $V_T=V\times_BT$ is a quasi-compact open subscheme of $T$. Since $\pi$ is integral, $Z\times_BT=Z\times_VV_T$ is represented by a scheme integral, hence affine, over $V_T$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Covering $V_T$ by finitely many affine opens, their inverse images are finitely many affine opens covering $Z\times_BT$; so this scheme is quasi-compact, and its identity is a representable surjective etale map from a quasi-compact scheme. Hence $f$ is quasi-compact; this is the transitivity-of-fibre-products argument of Tag 03HG.

proof.text: By [lem-a1-space-open-chart-tests], the representable open immersion $j$ is representable etale. Apply [lem-sfb-space-integral-factorization-etale-base-change] with $W=V$. Since $j$ is a monomorphism and $f=j\pi$, the projection $Z\times_B V\to Z$ is an isomorphism, with inverse $z\mapsto(z,\pi(z))$ on scheme-valued sections. Therefore the pulled-back factorization is $Z\xrightarrow{a}E_V\xrightarrow{\nu_V}V$, where $E_V=E\times_BV$, $\nu_V$ is integral, and this factorization has the same unique factorization property over $V$.

Use the universal property from [lem-sfb-space-integral-factorization-etale-base-change] in step 4 with the integral map $\pi:Z	o V$ and $\mathrm{id}_Z$. It gives $h:E_V	o Z$ with $ha=\mathrm{id}_Z$ and $\pi h=
u_V$. Both $ah$ and $\mathrm{id}_{E_V}$ are maps to the integral $V$-space $E_V$, have composite $a$ with $a:Z	o E_V$, and have composite $
u_V$ with $
u_V:E_V	o V$. Uniqueness gives $ah=\mathrm{id}_{E_V}$. Thus $a$ is an isomorphism over $V$, giving $E	imes_BV\simeq Z$. Finally $E_V	o E$ is the pullback of $j$: on a scheme test $T	o E$ it is the open subscheme $T	imes_BV\subseteq T$, so it is an open immersion by the definition of representable open immersion. Transport along $a$ identifies it with $Z\hookrightarrow E$.
